decision_rule: At width 280, the Pearson correlation between the main fit's predicted count and the true count is measured inside each bin of 35 label values. Any bin starting above label 175 that reaches 0.5 means wide counts ARE measurable. Otherwise, if every bin ending at or below label 140 reaches 0.5 and every bin starting above 175 stays below 0.2, wide counts are NOT represented. Any other pattern is RANGE_PATTERN_UNMATCHED. The bin from 141 to 175 is recorded and excluded.
metric: Pearson correlation between the main fit's predicted count and the true count, inside each bin of 35 label values at width 280.
notes: A correlation inside a bin, rather than a fit quality inside a bin, is what the design commits to here. A global fit's within-bin fit quality is bounded by one minus the squared ratio of the global residual spread to the bin's own spread, which for these numbers could not reach its own thresholds; the correlation has no such bound. The bin from 141 to 175 holds labels on both sides of 175, so it is recorded and left out of this decision. The decision uses the four bins ending at or below label 140 against the three bins starting above label 175. This check exists at width 280 only, as the design says, so it cannot classify a null wobble at width 200 on its own. Training pressure in this model's own corpus sits near 70 to 72 characters per line, which is context for a narrow measurable range, not a prediction. If the validity gate recorded in these values failed, this record is void as evidence about the model, and is an instrument fault only. A further run of this script on the same box is a rerun of the same instrument, not a replication.

values.statistic: Pearson correlation between predicted and true count
